# Plugins (details)

Full reference for every plugin. Read this on demand (e.g. before writing a helper or a test fixture, to check whether one already exists). A plugin's *Test helpers* item lists its `<runtime>/testing/` barrels: shared fixtures that only test code may import. The slim always-loaded index is [`plugins-compact.md`](./plugins-compact.md).

A list longer than 20 values (importers, uses, contributions) is summarized here and in the plugin's CLAUDE.md as one count per group; the linked `REFERENCE.md` beside the plugin lists it in full.

- **`active-data`** — Meta plugin for inline interactive widgets agents render via XML-like tags in assistant text. Sub-plugins contribute block (tag) and code (claimed code-span) renderers, and declare inline chips through primitives/text-editor/inline-chip; hosts use useActiveDataSegments() + useActiveDataLinkify(). Persistent state for inline interactive widgets — table + resource keyed by (conversationId, messageId, tag, occurrenceIndex).

    - **`go`** — Renders <go>…</go> in an agent's reply — a part of the answer the user can pick as their reply — as one tinted unit, [text | ▶]: ▶ sends it back as <go>…</go> (the agent reads the part of its answer the user picked), clicking the text puts it in the draft as an editable tinted region closed by a ✕. One line is inline wherever it is written; a multi-line block is a card with a ✎ / ▶ rail, its `- [ ]` lines pickable rows, or a table whose rows lead with `[ ]` / `[x]` a pickable table (only the picked items are sent — a row as a `- [x]` line of its first cell — and Reset restores the agent's picks). The user's sent message shows the accepted <go> in full, in the same tint.
      - Web:
        - Contributes:
          - `ActiveData.Tag` "go" → `GoBlock`
          - `InlineTextWalkerSlot`
          - `TextEditorSlots.Plugin` → `GoRegionPlugin`

    - **`id-chip`** — Id chips, web half: idChip({ presenter, surfaces, component? }) mints a kind's IdKinds.Presenter together with its inline chip — the pattern derived from the kind (never re-typed), a generic title + icon chip unless the family brings its own component, optionally carrying a first-meeting hint (declared to the hints engine, anchored on and requested by every resolved chip). rowReferent folds a live by-id row read into a presenter's referent state. Id chips, server half: idChipServer({ kind, surfaces, resolve }) contributes the kind's IdKinds.Referent, the InlineTokenReferentSource that hands a model the referent's title, and — for a chip that belongs in documents — the Editor.InlineToken that keeps a page block holding it agent-readable.

    - **`chord`** — Chord — a chord ear trainer that plays loops of real songs whose chords you have turned on, asks you to name each chord, and keeps track of how well you know each one.
      - Cross-plugin:
        - Imported by: `apps/chord/song-index`
      - Plugins:
        - **`curriculum`** — The curriculum's browser half: useCurriculum (the live chord.curriculum selection — each chord practised, heard or off, the blanks, how many other chords a loop may hold), useCatalog (the live chord.catalog), useCurriculumWrites (chords, blanks, extras; refusals as toasts), and <ChordsSection> — the trainer side panel's collapsible Chords section: Clear / Undo clear, the Blanks and Other-chords-per-loop pills, and every chord of the song index in tracks and sections, each chip cycling off → hear → practise, one chip per section's rare chords, and a footer giving the exact numbers of the chip under the pointer. The Chord trainer's curriculum, server side: the chord_curriculum row (each chord practised, heard or off; how much of a loop is blank; how many other chords a loop may hold), the live chord.curriculum resource and its three writes — chords, blanks, extras —, the live chord.catalog: every chord of the song index in tracks and sections, built once per loaded index, and the live chord.curriculum.loops: the trainer's loop find over the stored selection.

        - **`shell`** — App shell for the Demo sandbox: registers the /demo app entry — equin rendered in-process on made-up data (DemoScope + AppEmbed over the workspace demo's browser host), starting on its home app (the app gallery). Where the visitor is inside the demo is the page's URL, kept by the embed itself (its embed tail: /demo/at/<location>, e.g. /demo/at/agents/c/<id>), so a reload comes back to it; ;full=1 shows it maximized instead of framed under the caption bar (its Maximize button; a hover strip at the top edge reveals Restore, and Esc restores when nothing inside the demo wants it — both run as a view transition, and a 'Press Esc to restore' notice shows a few seconds), and a new browser tab opened from inside the demo opens it there, maximized, on the same data — with no second Enter equin, since the visitor is in the demo already. A maximized URL opened fresh (a reload) shows its gate maximized, so Enter opens the demo in place. Maximized, the demo is the tab: its moves are history entries (Back / Forward step through them, the embed following the URL); framed, they rewrite the current entry, so Back leaves the page. The /demo page's head script (DocumentHead.Fragment): starts the demo's browser host before the app boots, so its worker boots alongside the page's own bundle.

      - Plugins:
        - **`analytics`** — Umbrella for cookieless site analytics on deployed compositions: the host-only route guard, the collect half that ships inside the deployed site (ingest, tables, nightly rollup, retention, the report and its mirror set), and the dashboard half in the local deploy app, which runs that report on its copy of the site's tables.
          - Plugins:
            - **`collect`** — The visit tracker a deployed site mounts, cookieless unless the visitor consents: <AnalyticsTracker app={…} /> records one pageview per path change under that app (landing referrer and utm tags on the first only) and the visible time on each; track(name, props?) records a custom event on the current page; useSectionReach(section) / observeSectionReach(el, section) record section_reach once when a section reaches the upper half of the screen, its section prop (<page>/<key>) giving a per-section reach funnel; useAnalyticsConsent() / setAnalyticsConsent(accepted) read and answer the site's consent prompt — accepting keeps a random key in the browser for 13 months, sent with every pageview and event so a return is recognised on any network. Owns the analytics tables (daily salts kept 30 days with the hash → visitor links that let a returning visitor keep one id, 90-day visits and hits, forever daily totals at every single-filter level and forever per-visit memberships for exact unique visitors over any range), the public collect endpoint, the analytics mirror set, the report (runAnalyticsQuery) and the visit-list reads (a window of individual visits with their hits, filtered in the filter language) — both run by the deploy app on its local copy of the tables — the nightly analytics.rollup job and the visits retention sweep that refuses to delete a day not yet rolled up.
              - Server:
                - Contributes:
                  - `table-mirror-set` "analytics"

            - **`dashboard`** — Analytics tab of a site's page, shown only when the deployment's composition ships the collect plugin: range and comparison controls, KPI tiles choosing a trend line with a dashed previous period, ranked Pages / Sources / Locations / Devices / Events panels whose rows filter the whole dashboard (one filter on ranges past the raw window), and what one visit records.             - **`sessions`** — Sessions tab of a site's page, shown only when the deployment's composition ships the collect plugin: one row per anonymous visit (country, time, device and software, source, first visit or returning, channel), its journey on a shared log time axis (pages split by their share of the visit, the read line and section ticks, action icons, each named on hover) with its duration and actions; opening a row shows its timeline (each page, the sections reached and when, the actions in order, the exit). Read from this computer's copy of the site's analytics (site-mirror, its freshness line above the list; loading until a first whole copy is in place) as live key-range pages: the views (All / With actions / 2+ pages / Bounced) are saved filters, and every filter — whose visits, the device, any field — runs on the copy, a narrowed view carried in the URL. Serves a deployment's visits (deploy-analytics.sessions) from this computer's copy of the site's analytics tables (site-mirror's replica): collect's own visit-list SQL — the window, the rows by key, the groupings and the count, each filter compiled by collect — run on the copy, re-read whenever a pull applies a page to it.

Shown only when the composition needs a secret. Deploy-secret approvals on the local machine: values in the secrets store (namespace deploy-secrets), per-deployment grants of a value's HMAC fingerprint (deploy_secret_grants), the deploy gate that ends a run needs-approval while any secret its composition's closure declares is missing, new or changed, the deploy-secrets.status live value behind the Secrets section (each row with this computer's counterpart, from DeploySecrets.LocalValue, previewed — masked for a credential — never its value), the Use-this-computer's-value endpoint that stores it through the same write as Set value, and the browser-refusing endpoint converge reads the approved env from.

        - **`deployments`** — Sites — the Deploy app's primary entity, a deployment: the sites index (the app's landing page, a DataView of every deployment with its server and status), the site page (site/:deploymentId/:tab?) — a header (mark, hostname, status pill, hostnames, composition, contributed SiteHeader actions), the production strip (SiteStrip cells, its Server cell this plugin's own) with the first applicable SiteBanner, and the SiteTabs host bound to the URL's :tab?, whose Overview (a two-column host over SiteOverview.Card plus a Checks card over SiteCheck) and Settings (the DeploymentDetail sections — General, Install and a Danger zone of its own — under a left anchor rail) tabs are this plugin's, the sidebar's Overview entry and Sites section (status dot per site from useSiteStatus, + opening the add dialog), and the Deployments section of a server's page (that server's sites as a DataView, an add affordance whose composition picker reads the compositions config, a Deploy row action that launches the CLI's whole converge-build-ship run). Old server/:serverId/dep/:deploymentId links forward to the site. Owns the deploy_deployments table: where a composition is served and under what URL ((composition × server) → { hostnames, loopbackPort }), its live collection, and the CRUD endpoints. Also launches `./equin deploy converge|ship` for a deployment — and orchestrates the `update` sequence (converge → build a candidate unless one is already current → ship that pinned run id) over the awaitable release engine — streaming the CLI's output into the durable `deploy` log channel, each run's phase and outcome into the in-memory `deploy.runs` live view, and every run into the durable `deploy_runs` ledger it serves back as a live history window — the record that survives the restart the live view does not. Before any leg spawns, every DeployGates.Gate contribution is asked; a run one of them refuses ends needs-approval having converged and shipped nothing. The install itself — run user, dir layout, systemd unit, Caddy site — is derived in core/, never stored.

        - **`host-query`** — The deploy app's shared pieces for a section that reads its deployment's box over SSH: HostQueryFailureState renders every way the read can fail (no SSH key, unverified host, SSH failure, failed request, unreadable answer) in one vocabulary, and useDeploymentShips(deploymentId, pluginId) answers whether the deployment's composition closure includes a plugin (useShipsGate: the tab gate over it — shown unless the answer is no). hostOnlyQueryOverSsh(deploymentId, path, schema, { maxAnswerBytes? }): resolves a deployment's server and pinned SSH target, curls one host-only route of the install through its own gateway on the loopback port (two SSH sessions at most), refuses an answer over maxAnswerBytes unread (curl --max-filesize on the box, re-checked here), and answers the parsed answer, which of SSH, the request or the answer failed, or not-found. markServerBoxIsThisInstance(serverId) marks a demo's server whose box is this instance: its host-only routes are answered through this instance's own gateway, no SSH (the same answer cap applies).

            - **`intake`** — useSendSiteMessage() — the contact form's send (sent or rate-limited); a site takes messages by importing this barrel, which pulls the intake's server half into its composition. Owns site_messages: the public POST /api/site-messages endpoint (body capped at 8 KB; honeypot, a send under three seconds or a bot user agent stored as spam and still answered sent; 3 per 10 minutes and 10 per day per salted IP hash, the IP never stored), the site-messages.notify job emailing each accepted message through Resend from the approved RESEND_API_KEY deploy secret (not-configured without one, at most 30 emails a day, the rest held and counted in the next), the site-messages.confirm job emailing the visitor a copy so they know it arrived (at most 30 a day and 3 a day per address), the 30-day spam sweep, and the site_messages mirror set the deploy app copies (ip_hash omitted, the salt never mirrored).

        - **`sync`** — MessageBodyState: one message's mail.message-body value with its loading and failed-fetch (Retry) states drawn once, for every pane that shows a body. Gmail sync engine (on-demand model): a bounded, metadata-only backfill mirrors a recent window of message envelopes; history.list incremental delta keeps them fresh (with a bounded full-resync fallback on historyId expiry) via a scheduled main-only delta tick (the documented no-polling exception). Message bodies + attachments are hydrated lazily on first open by the mail.hydrate job (asked for by a mail.message-body subscriber, or POST /api/mail/hydrate to retry) and cached; the mail.message-body value reads one message's body state from the mirror. The mail.search paged value answers a Gmail search as ranked thread ids, mirroring the envelopes it sees. Mirrors threads/messages/labels into the mail-core tables.

Its ;page param, /places;page=<pageId>, lays one page's places over the same map, read live (page-overlay): the page's saved places numbered, the rest dimmed, the page's places not saved yet as numbered ghost pins, the camera framed on the page, the map never remounted — and a panel in the side panel's spot listing them in page order (hover-linked with their pins, each place's card drilled in, Save and Save all with one Undo, × back to the plain map).         - **`present`** — Open in a new tab on every gallery card (its live present page) and two frame actions on every prototype canvas frame: Open in a new tab (the frame's chromeless present page at the Responsive size, filling the tab at its own width; a source frame opens its own href) and Full screen (F, which presents the selected frame; the browser's Fullscreen API). While presenting, hovering shows the frame's tag (the canvas frame header's own box: options chip | version stepper) and 'i of n', Exit and the size & zoom chip, on the right edge + (add a frame) and Compare with each resolved frame source (the real app, swiped) — both adding the frame and leaving to the prototype's canvas in the app — and the left and right arrow keys flip through the canvas's frames. The new tab is present/<id>/<sha|live>/<declared|size word>/<picks?>, a one-frame page carrying the frame's version and own picks, with an Exit icon back to the prototype's canvas; its + / Compare open the app's canvas on the frame plus the new one.

        - **`player`** — Sonata player: SonataPlayerScope, the one composition root of a player (cursor store > song document > playback session > player view, with the per-session effects and a library song's setting observers), and the parts a host composes inside it — PlayerDisplay, PlayerTransport (the strip row of every Transport contribution: play, scrubber, loop), PlayerTime. Owns the SonataPlayer.{Display,Transport,Effect} slots — Effect mounting once per player while a PlayerDisplay shows it (the keyboard transport) — and the per-player view state (display lens, piano-roll spread, shown, drawn — each display reports when it has drawn with useMarkDisplayDrawn), whose display pick a host can bind to its own value (a URL param) with PlayerDisplayBinding.

        - **`recording`** — Sonata recording: the session's recording player — the YouTube video whoever shows a song's recording declares (useShowRecording), owned by the playback session so it outlives what shows it: RecordingVideo is only a viewport the playing iframe is moved into (Element.moveBefore, never reloaded) and out of, to an off-screen parking spot, so collapsing its section or switching the display neither stops nor reloads it. When the open score is timed on that video (Score.meta.recording) it is the session's transport driver while ready — the cursor, the synth and the A–B loop follow the video, its rate is the tempo; otherwise it plays on its own with YouTube's controls under a “Not synced” badge. RecordingSwitch turns the video off (the synth plays alone, same timing) and on. The video's on/off persists in the sonata.recording-video config; its sound, level and the sync offset (no control in the card; Settings → Config) in the sonata.recording config. Owns the SonataRecording.Refused seam for whoever picked a video YouTube refuses to embed. Server registration of the Sonata recording mix config and the video on/off config.

        - **`sources`** — Input source sub-plugins for Sonata (MIDI, chord-grid, …).
          - Plugins:
            - **`chord-grid`** — Chord-grid input source for Sonata. A small mini-language (e.g. `Amaj9 Am9 (E E6)`) authors chord annotations: each cell is a bar, a `( )` group shares a bar, and `.` holds the previous chord. A cell may name a chord by letter (`Am7`) or by degree (`vi7`), the latter resolved against the key a `key:` directive declares. compile() emits chord + key annotations only; the shell's reactive re-voicing step generates the notes under the global voicing config. Persists per-song grid text and contributes the library 'New Chord Grid' affordance, hydration, the cell of the Chords field its extension exposes on every list of songs, the song cover (its first chords as degree-coloured chord boxes), and an in-player editor section. Owns the sonata_songs_ext_chord_grid side-table: per-song chord text. Creates chord-grid–backed songs, persists grid edits (syncing the parent song's derived duration only; the title is library-owned), and exposes the chord text to every list of songs (LiveColumns.Expose) for its Chords field and cover.
              - Web:

            - **`ultimate-guitar`** — Player-side Ultimate Guitar source for Sonata: paste a UG tab URL, fetch its raw tab, and compile() the chord/lyric markup into a playable Score (lyric-proportional, bar-quantized timing synthesis → chord annotations, sections, lyrics, synthesized 4/4 tempo). Reading UG itself (a tab, the catalog search) is the machine/ half's.

        - **`transcription`** — Sonata transcription in the library: a 'Transcribe…' entry in the + menu (a video/post link, or page images and PDFs) that creates the song and starts the transcribing agent; a transcribed song shows its agent run as an embedded agent thread — the steps, the agent's summary and a reply box — in the player until the score is in (Retry when it failed), then in the player's Transcription section, where a reply asks for a correction and the resubmitted score replaces the song's; and a Transcribing / Failed badge and cover on its card. Owns the sonata_songs_ext_transcription side-table: a transcribed song's run state (status, input, task, latest conversation, error). POST transcribe creates the song (MusicXML source), a Sonata task and a transcribing agent in a `sonata.transcription` scratch workspace (CLAUDE.md = the instructions, ./bin/st = the toolkit); its sonata_submit_transcription MCP tool imports the agent's MusicXML into the song. Exposes its status, latest conversation and error to every list of songs (LiveColumns.Expose); a conversation closed before submitting marks the song failed (retry relaunches).
          - Web:

            - **`screenshot`** — Landing demo band: equin itself, live, where the desktop picture was — its real server code in a worker on the workspace demo's data (DemoScope around AppEmbed), entered through Enter equin on every visit (a first visit downloads nothing before it; a browser already holding the data starts the host behind it; a maximized URL shows the gate maximized; a tab opened while the visitor is in the demo in another tab joins it with no gate, its frame grown). Entering grows the frame in place for good, nearly as wide and tall as the window; once it runs, Maximize (a view transition over the tab's surface, above the site; Restore at its top edge, a 'Press Esc to restore' notice, Esc) and Reset demo sit under it. Where the visitor is inside the demo, and whether it is maximized, is the homepage's URL, kept by the embed itself (/about/at/<location>[;full=1]; old ;view.website.demo=… links are rewritten onto it), with the embed's history rule: framed, moves rewrite the current entry; maximized, they are the tab's history.

    - **`app-embed`** — <AppEmbed app? route? onLeave? fills? onTitleChange? />: the app rendered in-process inside its own box — an embedded tab set (TabsProvider embedded: seeded from the page URL's place, else app + route, else the composition's home app — non-live stores never touching the page URL, history or storage, none of the page's signals) and the same surface body the app's layout renders, so pane opens, app switches and the Desktop (its windows the embed's own tabs) work as in the app. Its navigation boundary resolves URLs against the apps in scope: an app's URL moves the embed, a surface-mode app's base path switches its mode, anything else is onLeave (default: a toast). Its theme scope is the focused tab's app's (transform-gpu, so fixed chrome stays in the embed); solo fills the embed box, and it opens docked. It keeps its own place in the page URL — the enclosing pane's embed tail, <the page URL>/at/<location>[;full=1] — so a host writes no URL code — never a place no one chose (nothing is written until the user moves it); framed, a move rewrites the current history entry; maximized, each move is the entry the app's own tab would write; Back / Forward move it back; a new browser tab opened inside opens this page there, maximized. useEmbedPlace() gives the host's chrome maximized / setMaximized (a pushed entry) / reset. fills: page | viewport: it is all the page shows (takes the keyboard at mount); a viewport-filling one hosts the page's floating action bar. Its box is a reveal boundary (a reveal inside never scrolls the host page), and onTitleChange hands the host its focused tab's title (<Entity> — <App>). Knows nothing about demos or where data comes from.

- **`auth`** — Shared authentication infrastructure (OAuth 2.0, API keys, password sign-in). Exposes the Accounts pane — a DataView of every provider (Auth.Provider) and non-provider setup surface (Auth.Integration), grouped by service, each row opening one account pane to the right (header, account, and the row's setup inline — a provider's setup wizard, OAuth client steps or sign-in form; an integration's own setup) — and the Settings app surfaces the Account entry. Worktree-side auth helpers. Provides getTokenFromCentral() for worktree plugins that need OAuth tokens. Centralized OAuth/API-key/password-sign-in infrastructure for third-party services. Tokens persist via the central secrets store; auth runs on the central runtime so all worktrees share one connected state.

- **`backup`** — Backup orchestrator UI: run backups, view history, and open one run's detail pane — whose sections (what went into the archive, where it was dispatched to, and the Grant access repair for a target that lost its OAuth token) are contributed by the backup arm. Backup orchestrator: assembles archives from registered backup sources, dispatches to registered storage targets. The assembly runs OUT OF PROCESS as a supervised job's `run` body, so a backend restart mid-`tar` no longer kills the backup.

    - **`runs-arm`** — The backup arm's presence on the merged run surface: its rows' link into the backup run-detail pane, its four scalar columns (native status, archive size, source and target counts) as real filterable and sortable SQL dimensions, and the three detail sections — the archive's size on one line, the manifest's source reports, and the per-target outcome with its Grant access remediation. The backup arm of the unified run space: binds backup_runs into the runs union — its native status folded into the shared outcome vocabulary (partial included, since backup is the only kind that can half-succeed), a label naming what the run covered, and the source / target counts plus the raw per-target results as its own columns. Reads null for namespace (a backup covers the machine, not a checkout — the table's own namespace column is the in-flight index's scope discriminator, not a fact about the run) and for message (a backup's failure words are per-target).

    - **`agent-thread`** — Agent thread: the embedded conversation view apps host for the background agents they start — <AgentThread> (user bubbles, the agent's tool calls as a live step list labelled through the AgentThreadSlots.StepLabel dispatch, its answer, the host's own result cards, a composer that resumes an ended conversation), EndThreadButton (Close ×: close the conversation and drop its task — always there, so an ended thread still closes), the hooks a host's other surfaces read (useThreadTurns, useThreadProgress, useLatestResult), generic step labels for the common built-in tools, and useThreadRuns (a host's recent runs under its scratch profile). Serves `agent-thread.runs` — the recent conversations launched in a scratch workspace, newest first, filterable by profile — over `_conversations` with the attempt joined (routed: a conversation write refills its own row).

    - **`all-conversations`** — All-conversations app pane: a live DataView over the `conversations.all` collection (filter/sort/search over every conversation, kept fresh by the routed change feed) reachable from the agent-manager sidebar; and how the conversations entity's fields present in every conversation list (the optimistic status cell, the model filter's live catalog options). Serves the two conversation-list collections — `conversations.all` (system conversations hidden by a default scope) and `conversations.history` — over `_conversations` with the owner joins (attempt → task), routed: a conversation, attempt or task write refills only the rows it changes.

        - **`pending-turn`** — The single entry point for sending a turn from the browser (useSendConversationTurn, bound to the subtree's transport: mints the turn's ledger id, shows its echo at once, then runs its delivery), and the view of the server's turn ledger (conversations/turn-ledger): usePendingTurns merges a conversation's live ledger rows with this tab's sends whose row has not arrived, PendingTurnCard renders each by state (echo while held or being typed until the transcript holds its line, Retry + Copy to draft when it failed), useSentTurnFollowKey is the transcript's followKey (moves only when the user sends a turn, never on an automatic event turn or a retiring echo), and useOptimisticConversationStatus reads a conversation as working from the instant a turn is sent. Every surface (prompt input, template chips, Send/Queue/Go, Push & Close, AskUserQuestion answers) sends through it and differs only in its delivery. Contributes the turn-send-safety lint rule.

    - **`runtime-sdk`** — The health report's Claude Code row: Claude Code itself (critical while the computer is signed out, with the in-app Sign in — claude-cli/sign-in, 'Signing in…' while it runs — and Check again), the agent processes running — here, and in every other worktree (each as its task's chip) — the active Claude account's usage limits as meters (named by the account; the week collapsed, the session too expanded; attention while its limit is reached), the conversations an API error stopped (Resume all), and Manage accounts. The agent manager's sidebar foot: the Claude account new agents launch on with its weekly quota, opening the account menu (its session and week meters; each account's weekly room, add — signing in to another account in the app, or an API key — / remove / switch, auto-switch, auto-resume when a limit resets, Continue on another account when the active one is limited). The sdk runtime's portable half: the conversations_ext_sdk_agent side table (each agent's event cursor and the projection of its events — session id, busy/idle, the open question, the last turn and its rewind anchor — out of the change feed, being the consumer's per-batch checkpoint) and the conversations_ext_sdk_agent_stop side table (the part a live surface reads: the API-error stop and the account, written only when it changes), the pure event reducer, and the mapping of a launch onto the agent's options file; the runtime-sdk.error-stopped collection (active conversations whose agent's turn an API error stopped — a usage limit, a server error, a lost connection — with the CLI's kind of failure); the auto-resume setting (Resume agents when their usage limit resets).

The turn ledger's backend: the conversation_turns table (one row per turn sent to an agent, its state moved only by applyTurnEvent's pure transition), the accept that holds a turn while its conversation starts, confirmTurn (the agent's confirmation that it took a turn, applied to that row by the turn id it echoed, with the transcript line's uuid; resolvePromptSubmit is its temporary equality-matched fallback for an agent started before turn ids), Stop's and rewind's returnTurnByPromptUuid (the turn taken back, by its transcript line), the turn-ledger.turns live collection, the conversation.userTurnSent event (emitted once the agent confirmed a user's turn) and the 7-day retention sweep of settled rows.

    - **`connection`** — Every backend database connection, built one way: createDbPool / createDbClient give each pool or standalone client a name from the closed pool-name set and a pg.Client subclass that bounds connect() and every query() with a deadline (60 s, widened per scope by withQueryDeadline). A call with no reply rejects with QueryDeadlineExceededError (pool, phase, sql, origin), and its connection is closed — handed back to its pool as broken and its socket destroyed, so Postgres rolls back its transaction and PgBouncer frees its slot — and announced on queryDeadlineSink. A session the server ends for idling inside its transaction (25P03) is announced on idleTransactionEndedSink with the origin and statement of the transaction's last statement, and every later call on that connection fails with IdleTransactionEndedError. Every connection logs in as application_name equin:<pool> (equin-cli:<pool> from a process with no runtime namespace, which reports nothing). Every pool also carries its own connection-error listeners (pool and per client), which report a broken connection once instead of letting it crash the process — so a library handed the pool (graphile-worker) installs none of its own.
      - Core:
        - Uses: `framework/product-name.PRODUCT_NAME`

    - **`lane-isolation`** — The end-to-end proof that the app's connection lanes are isolated all the way down to PgBouncer: with every background server slot of a throwaway database held idle in a transaction (the 2026-11-03 shape), interactive queries still answer. Test only — a child of database so it can use the throwaway-database fixture, which itself depends on database.
    - **`lock-watch`** — Database lock watch: a per-worktree job that looks at pg_stat_activity + pg_blocking_pids once a minute (Postgres has no change signal for lock waits), on a held direct session that neither a saturated pgbouncer nor a stall of new connections can starve, and names every session holding others back or idle inside a transaction past 60 s by the origin its statement's comment carries — a db-lock-holder report (one row per origin) and the db-lock-watch push value behind the health report's Database row. Each look also probes a new connection; one still unanswered after 5 s gets a snapshot of every busy backend on the cluster, read on the held session, in db.jsonl. Its first look is enqueued at boot by a warm-up, so a restarted backend does not wait for the next minute. It never ends a session. Every session the cluster's idle-in-transaction timeout ends is reported (db-idle-transaction-ended, one row per origin): from the session's own client (database/connection's idleTransactionEndedSink, SQLSTATE 25P03) or, for a session no app client owns, from the watch seeing it gone between two looks with pg_stat_database.sessions_fatal up.
      - Server:

          - `report-kind` "db-idle-transaction-ended"

    - **`backend-crash`** — Backend death report renderers: one-line Debug → Reports summaries for backend-crash (worktree, signal, uptime, Bun's panic line), backend-exit (worktree, exit code, booting or how long after ready) and backend-crash-loop (worktree, deaths and span, causes, looping or ended). The backend death report kinds, filed by the gateway through the report outbox for every backend (central and main included) death it did not cause, drained by main: backend-crash (a signal it did not send — the signal, Bun's panic line and bun.report link, the macOS crash report's location), backend-exit (an exit code nobody asked for — the code, whether it died booting or serving) and backend-crash-loop (a worktree that keeps dying: the deaths, their causes, the last one's stderr), each with the dead process's last stderr lines. Main's own deaths are filed by the next main backend that lives long enough to drain the outbox.

Plus a debug-only trigger that freezes a worktree backend's JS thread to reproduce it. Backend liveness probe (central): every 15 s asks each running backend for any HTTP answer on its own socket, and appends a frozen episode to the backend-liveness data dir when one stays unanswered for a minute of awake time (machine sleep never counts; a stopped process is paused, not frozen) — from outside the backend, so a frozen JS thread is noticed while it lasts.

        - **`tab-memory`** — Tab memory telemetry, browser half: every top-level page the user drives samples itself (JS heap, DOM nodes, canvases, images, its open in-app tabs and route) 30 s after load and every 5 minutes after, posted to its own server; Debug → Tab memory draws each page beside each Chrome renderer's footprint (by pid) over the last 12 h, with a DataView of the pages; registers the climb watch's bars (tab-memory-climb) for Settings → Config. Tab memory telemetry, server half: logs each page's sample to the durable tab-memory channel of the worktree it talks to, and serves tab-memory.series — every worktree's pages over the last 12 h beside each Chrome renderer's footprint (by pid) from main's health-owners log. The climb watch: every 10 minutes on main, a Chrome renderer whose memory floor is too large or climbing files a tab-memory-climb report (error) with its growth curve, the pages alive through its window and what grew.

    - **`sentinel`** — Sentinel web presence: registers the sentinel config (sampler cadence + onset thresholds) for Settings → Config and the one-line duress-episode and sentinel-down report summaries for Debug → Reports. The health report's Machine watcher row is its health-row sub-plugin. Cluster congestion sentinel: a main-only always-on sampler + onset detector + duress-latch lifecycle on a dedicated worker thread (host load, Postgres-side wait/lock/IO pressure, fleet state, per-backend health rollup, compressor pressure), feeding the 'cluster' trace ring so every trace gains a cluster-vitals lane, congestion onset is observable, and the latch lease survives a wedged main loop. Persists duress episodes as trip/clear lines on the duress-episodes channel (readDuressEpisodes). Reports the watcher's own supervision status: a host-global status file written on every transition, served on every backend as the sentinel.status push resource (with the duress latch), and a sentinel-down report when main gives up respawning it.     - **`stuck-spans`** — Stuck-span report renderer: a one-line Debug → Reports summary for the span-stuck kind (how long it has been running, the chain of operations it is stuck under, and a View-trace chip). Stuck-span watchdog: a 15 s interval on each backend's own event loop — deliberately NOT a scheduled job — that reads the runtime profiler's open entries and files a span-stuck report while an http / sub / loader / push / flush / cascade span is still running past its threshold (90 s — past the app pool's 60 s query deadline; http 120 s), once per span run, naming the deepest stuck span of a chain with its open ancestors and attaching one coherent-instant trace per tick. Catches the hang a completion-time slow-op report never can. duressExempt; job and bg spans are excluded.

- **`framework`** — Umbrella for framework primitives: web plugin SDK, server, central
  - Plugins:
    - **`browser-server`** — A server that runs in the page's realm or across a worker's port — a third host of the unified live API (core: the BrowserServer interface; runtimeBrowserServer over a resource runtime booted in this realm; serveOverPort / portBrowserServer carrying one across a MessageChannel or a Web Worker). Web: browserServerTransport(server, { telemetry, frameBase }), the Transport a <TransportProvider> points a subtree at — in-memory sockets to its runtime, requests through its router, an inert central socket; attachFrameServing(worker, serviceWorkerUrl) serves the server's frame documents by URL through the host's frame-serving Service Worker (frames-sw.ts), giving the transport its frameBase. HostInputs.Supply: a plugin declares a value of the page's own server the page may hand a browser host (a page input). ExternalHosts.Declare: the third-party hosts a plugin's code loads from in the page, read statically into each browser host's externalHosts.

          - `inRealmServer` — A browser server over a resource runtime in this realm, wired as a browser host is (`bootBrowserHost` + `runtimeBrowserServer`): the served declarations, the given routes and `/api/resources/:key` through the shared router, any other `/api` request the unsupported refusal (`unmatchedApiResponse`).

        - **`demo`** — Demo scenarios for a browser server (core only): DemoScenario — the app, the route, and the browser host (DemoHost: the composition scope the page renders the demo in, and the worker whose real server code serves the story).
          - Core:
            - Exports (types):
              - `DemoHost`
              - `DemoScenario`
          - Plugins:
            - **`prestart`** — Which SharedWorker a demo's tabs share — its name, the scenario and its Reset generation (kept page-wide, so a Reset moves every tab past the closing worker) — and connecting a tab to it (connectDemoHost: never to a worker that is retiring — its generation is skipped — and the head start's connection when there is one), started before the page boots where the page says so (prestartDemoHost, run by the demo page's head script), so the host boots alongside the page's own bundle. Kept apart from demo/scope so that head script loads only this, not the scope's UI.
              - Web:
                - Uses: `primitives/dom/web-storage.defineStore`
                - Exports (types):
                  - `DemoHostConnection`
                  - `HostGenerations`
                - Exports (values):
                  - `connectDemoHost`

              - Cross-plugin:
                - Imported by: `framework/browser-server/demo/scope`
            - **`scope`** — <DemoScope scenario>: renders its subtree against the scenario's browser host — real server code in a worker, on the scenario's seed — and scoped to the host's composition (<PluginScope>), so the page shows exactly the plugins the worker serves. Everything inside reaches the host only (the scope's transport): the build's coverage guard holds the host to serving every read, endpoint and config the scope uses, or declaring it needsMachine (answered unavailable); a key or endpoint it still does not serve fails loudly. A host that fails to boot throws to the error boundary. An optional boot render gates the demo on every visit (DemoBoot: checking, the gate, then starting with the worker's progress): the visitor enters it (enter), or — while they are in the demo in another tab of this browser (a shared Web Lock each such tab holds) — the tab joins it with no gate (onEnter hears both, and which: the gate's click, or a join no one acted on); a page whose own URL says whether the visitor is in decides alone (resume: true — no gate, only the loading; false — the gate, no join); behind the gate, a browser already holding the demo's data starts the host at once, a first visit only on enter, since it downloads the whole server and its data. Connects to one SharedWorker per build (every tab of the demo shares its server and data: a worker that finds the same host serving under another name sends the tab there — it joins, never takes it), shows the true cause when the host will not serve the page (equin updated in another tab; a browser without SharedWorker that opened it in another tab), and exposes Reset (useDemoHostControl) — the host wipes its data and every tab reconnects to a fresh one.

      - Test helpers:
        - Core: `@plugins/framework/plugins/server-core/core/testing`
          - `bootPluginGraph` — Load the plugin graph, run `register`, collect contributions, run the `onReadyBlocking` barrier.
          - `clearCollectedContributions` — Forget what was collected — back to the pre-boot state.
          - `clearRelationBases` — Back to "not set" (test support: a suite that set bases must not leak them into the next).
          - `declaredHostServiceIds` — Every declared host service's id, sorted — test support (`core/testing`): what a graph whose modules are loaded must provide.
          - `getReadSetIndex` — The whole index as a plain object, each key's tables sorted — every key that ever captured a table, including one a removal emptied (`[]`).
          - `hostServicesProvidedBy` — The ids of the declared host services `contributions` provide, sorted — test support (`core/testing`), for a suite choosing a graph's providers.
          - `isHostService` — True IFF `value` is a service `defineHostService` made — test support (`core/testing`), for a suite reading which services a module exports.
          - `isolateHostServices` — Isolate this test file's declared host services: from here on no service is declared (so a graph the suite boots is not asked for the `bun test` preload's desktop providers, and the services the suite declares are its own), and once the file's tests are done the process's declared set comes back exactly as it was — the suite's own services gone, the preload's back for every later suite in the same bun process.
          - `removeReadSetTable` — Remove `table` from the read-set of every key EXCEPT those in `keepKeys` — the one eviction path of an append-only index (a suite isolating its own keys from another's captures).
          - `runPostReadyPhases` — The post-ready phases of a SERVING host (`serve`, `browser`): `onReady` (graph-driven: each plugin fires as soon as its `dependsOn` parents have resolved), then the `onAllReady` barrier. `exec` never runs them — a short-lived child has no subscribers, so no watcher, job runner or LISTEN belongs in it.
          - `runSettledPhase` — The settled phase of a SERVING host (`serve`, `browser`): every plugin's `onSettled`, once the host is already serving and every post-ready phase has resolved — post-serving catch-up work (infra/warmup drains every declared warm-up here). `exec` has no path to it: a short-lived child must never run heavy post-serving work, and this function is the only caller of the hook.
          - `serverEntries`
          - `serverEntryFor` — The registry entry of `pluginPath`'s server barrel, as codegen writes one (`<id>` the dotted path, loaded by its `@plugins/<path>/server` specifier), with the `dependsOn` the caller states and no core barrel to warm.
          - `setServerErrorHandler` — Route every `reportServerError` to `fn` — or to nobody (`null`) — discarding whatever was held before, so a suite never receives another suite's reports.
          - `withHostServices` — Run `fn` with `providers` (each a `Svc.provide(impl)`) answering their services — over the unbooted host's providers and over a collected graph's — and put the previous answers back once it settles, so a suite swapping a service cannot leak it into the suites after it in the same bun process.

    - **`attachments`** — Polymorphic file attachments. Exposes uploadAttachment() helper; storage/serve on the server plugin. Attachments: rows plus bytes in the host's blob store (AttachmentBlobs — on the desktop UUID-named files under ~/.equin/state/attachments/). Consumers declare ownership with Attachments.defineLink(ownerTable, linkRef) over a link entity their own core declares, serve its scoped link collection and contribute it as Attachments.Link — attachments.by-owner follows each contributed set (built at bind), naming no owner; orphan sweep reclaims unreferenced rows past TTL. holdAttachments keeps an attachment an unsent draft references alive for the draft's lifetime.

    - **`background`** — Umbrella for what the app runs on its own: the catalog every background mechanism reports into, and the page that lists it.
      - Plugins:
        - **`catalog`** — Background activity catalog, browser half: the live read of one entry across both halves of the catalog, the countdown to its next run, and the catalog list (a DataView grouped by kind, with status, trigger in words, next and last run) and entry detail (scope, declaring plugin, recent runs with a row-action slot the mounting app fills, Run now) components — mounted as panes by Debug → Background activity. Background activity catalog: defineBackgroundKind registers a provider (a mechanism that runs things on its own: jobs, warm-ups, timers) that lists its entries with trigger, scope and latest run, its recent runs and an optional Run now; the catalog merges every provider into the pushed background.catalog value (throttled), serves background.recent-runs per entry and POST /api/background/run-now, fills event-triggered entries' event names from contributed BackgroundTriggerSource annotations, and names no provider. Background activity catalog, central half: defineBackgroundKind registers a provider for what the machine-wide central runtime runs on its own, merged into the pushed background.central-catalog value (every entry scope central) with background.central-recent-runs per entry.

    - **`claude-cli`** — Consumer half of the claude-cli call log: useClaudeCliCalls({correlationId, occurredAt}) answers 'which model calls produced this record?' as a calls / none / not-retained result, <ClaudeCliCallDetail> is the one rendering of a recorded call (header, meta grid, context with id chips, output or error, prompt, system — each copyable), and SLOW_CALL_MS is the duration past which a call reads as slow. One-shot Claude generations for short, latency-tolerant work (runClaudePrint), and runClaudeReadOnly — a turn that may only Read / Grep / Glob one directory and answers with a zod-schema'd structured value. Each is one Agent SDK turn (infra/claude-cli/sdk) on the active Claude account — the one new agents launch on — recorded in the call log.

    - **`endpoints`** — Typed endpoint contract primitive. useFetchEndpoint (a FetchEndpoint bound to the subtree's transport; fetchEndpointOver(t) for sanctioned page-level code) and useEndpointMutation send writes only — a GET def is a tsc error (the derived read marker; & WriteEndpoint) and throws if cast through (every server read is a live resource, read with useLive, or useLiveReader in an event handler); useAssetSrc turns an AssetPath (a GET endpoint's asset) into what an element loads over the subtree's transport (the path, a blob URL, or unavailable); useAssetUrl / assetUrlOver hand a sink that loads by URL on its own (a library's fetch, an HTML string) an AssetPath's or AssetBase's URL, unavailable, or fetch-only (served, but no URL reaches it); assetFetchOver hands a library that takes a fetch hook the asset's base and a fetch over the transport; contentUrlOver hands a content frame a ContentPath's URL on the transport's content serving (the content host, off every app origin, for the page's own server; an in-browser server's frame Service Worker, declared safe), unavailable, or unsupported. Typed endpoint contract primitive. defineEndpoint declares the contract; implement() creates the server handler; callEndpoint() calls one from off the page (a backend, the CLI) through its contract; useFetchEndpoint / useEndpointMutation consume it on the client. Typed endpoint contract primitive, central half: implementCentral() creates central's handler of an endpoint declared needsMachine — central runs only on the computer, so it serves what a host without one answers not available.

    - **`file-watcher`** — defineFileWatcher: the one declared in-process file watcher — a named, described declaration (static policy: extensions, ignore, debounce, ceiling, writesWhileOpen, depth, mainOnly) whose start({dirs, label, onChange, onLost}) — start({files, …}) for a writesWhileOpen one, which follows writes to the named files only (kqueue on darwin, one descriptor per file; every follow of a directory shares one subscription) — opens instances over one @parcel/watcher engine (debounce + ceiling flush; no timer — a dropped event is reported to onLost, the one backstop). Records per declaration its open instances, last change batch and a ring of handler runs for the Background activity catalog (onWatcherActivity / listFileWatchers / fileWatcherRecentRuns). The cli barrel's watchForCommand is the same engine for a foreground command, with no registry. acquireDirWatch({dir, scope, onChange}) is the shared directory-watch hub: refcounted native watches, a dir under a watched root riding its watch (a watcher never moved off a live root: a root opening above leaves it where it is), with subtree or children (depth-1 listing) scope — a children request with no root above it opening only a single-directory watch (depth children), never a recursive one. On macOS a children watch is kqueue's (a descriptor on the dir and each entry, budgeted — a dir past the budget rides FSEvents), so watching / or ~ puts nothing on fseventsd; every other FSEvents watch with no ignore rides the process's stream pool — one stream per watched root, a dir under an open recursive stream riding it, whatever declaration asks (fsEventsStreams reads it).
      - Cross-plugin:

Each root's folder is a location in this host's file system (DataFilesImpl.location: the data dir on the computer's disk, or the same dir in the browser storage's hidden data folder), where file-systems' reads read its files.     - **`ssh`** — Hermetic SSH client primitive: sshRun (one remote command) and sshUpload (one file, over scp) open a session to (host, port, user) with EXACTLY the private key they are given — IdentitiesOnly + IdentityAgent=none + -F /dev/null keep the machine's own agent, config and multiplexed sessions out, so a connection test proves the key it was handed works — and return a discriminated result whose failures are classified from OpenSSH stderr (dns / unreachable / timeout / auth / host-key-mismatch / command-failed / unknown). Both are built from one shared hermetic invocation, so the isolation flags cannot drift between them. Host-key policy is pinned-or-learn with no 'off'; the key is materialized 0600 into a mkdtemp dir removed in finally. An upload lands on a staging sibling and is renamed over its destination, so it can neither fail because the destination is being executed nor leave a truncated file where a working one was.
      - Cross-plugin:
        - Imported by:
          - `apps/deploy/health`
          - `apps/deploy/host-query`

    - **`trash`** — Web seam of the trash primitive: useUndoableTrash() runs a trashing mutation and records ONE entry on the tab's undo stack (undo = restore the minted trash entry, redo = re-trash and re-capture the new entry id), so every trash source gets Cmd+Z restore without hand-rolling it. Generic trash primitive: the trash_entries operation ledger, a defineTrashSource registry, list/restore/purge endpoints, the trash-entries live collection (filterable by source) and the 30-day purge sweep (a nightly retention job running each source's purge before the ledger rows go) — so user content is soft-deleted (restorable) instead of hard-deleted, and FK cascades fire only at purge.

    - **`youtube`** — Embedded YouTube player the app controls: loadYouTubeIframeApi (the IFrame API, loaded once), <YouTubePlayer controller videoId loop autoplay audio onReady onPlaying onError onStateChange/> bound to a useYouTubePlayer() controller (without controls the iframe takes no pointer and its thumbnail covers it until it first plays, so none of YouTube's chrome shows, and a click opens the video on youtube.com at the playhead) (play, pause, isPlaying, isAdvancing, playRange for one pass then back to the loop, seek — re-cueing a video that has not started rather than starting it — getCurrentTime, getDuration, getPlaybackRate, setPlaybackRate resolving to the rate the video took), useYouTubePlayerState, useYouTubePlayhead (one read per animation frame while playing), and createMediaClock (a smoothed, slewed reading of the playhead for something slaved to it). Loops without polling: one timer to the loop's end, reset on every state change. Server-side YouTube: checkOembed(videoId) asks oEmbed whether a video plays in an embed (status code mapped by the core's statusFromOembedCode, plus the title and channel of a 200), and searchYouTube(query, exec) lists YouTube's results for a query (id, title, channel, duration, views, verified, art track) through yt-dlp's flat search, from the on-demand `youtube-audio` dependency this plugin owns.

        - **`audio-fetch`** — YouTube audio download: fetchYouTubeAudio(videoId, exec) returns one video's best audio stream as served (webm/opus or m4a, no ffmpeg), downloaded by yt-dlp — JavaScript challenges solved on bun — from the on-demand `youtube-audio` Python dependency into a host-wide cache under a per-video host flock; a hit is a file read. A video YouTube will not serve throws YouTubeAudioUnavailableError (non-retryable); a stream YouTube refuses (HTTP 403, intermittent) is re-extracted with a freshly signed URL and retried up to 3 times; still refused, or another download error of the video, throws YouTubeAudioDownloadError — isYouTubeAudioError answers 'the video's failure, not the machine's' for both. A bot check, rate limit or unreachable YouTube throws YouTubeAccessError (retryable, the machine's failure). Failures come back from the Python module as a classified document, never a traceback. The daily youtube-audio.sweep keeps the cache within 30 days unused and 2 GB.
          - Server:

              - `YouTubeAccessError` — This machine cannot get audio from YouTube right now, whatever the video: a bot check or rate limit on its IP (`blocked`), or YouTube cannot be reached (`network`).
              - `YouTubeAudioDownloadError` — This video's download failed in a way that may clear later: YouTube still refused its audio stream (HTTP 403) after re-extracting it, or another download error on this video (a broken format).
              - `YouTubeAudioUnavailableError` — YouTube will not serve this video to anyone: unavailable, private, removed, age-gated.

- **`map`** — Vendor-neutral map primitive: <MapView overlays/> draws pins, paths and areas through the first GeoMap.Renderer (showing its set-up action while it is blocked, and a loud state when none is installed), with every pin's look contributed through the GeoMap.Pin dispatch slot keyed on its pinType, and a crowd mode the caller picks: clustering (every group of nearby pins drawn through the GeoMap.Cluster dispatch slot keyed on the pinType its pins share) or spots (every pin stays drawn — far out as a compact centred mark, with the size of each spot beside its lead pin). - **`menu-bar`** — The menu-bar panel the native helper opens: the menu-bar app (unlisted, colorMode light — the panel is designed light) mounted at /home/menu-bar, whose whole layout is the panel (no pane; chromeless under ?embed=1), whose body is the MenuBar.Section slot, drawn in its own theme (a native menu's: the system font, 13px rows, a 2–16px spacing ramp, the menu palette), plus the header (the spiral and a status line joined from MenuBar.Status parts, whose attention lights the menu-bar icon's dot) and the footer ('Running · <host>', opening equin). useNativeHost() reads the helper's bridge (window.equinNative): pending, absent (a plain browser), or present with its platform, capabilities and methods — a capability the host lacks has no method. useNativeApps() reads the device's installed and pinned apps from the helper that keeps them (pending / unavailable / ready / error), re-read on panel focus and after a pin. usePanelInput() is the panel's typed text (the task field writes it, the app grid filters by it), kept as a draft across reloads. - **`network`** — Umbrella for how data moves between the server and the browser: the live-resource API (declare a collection, query it, serve it) and, later, the live-state primitives it is built on.
  - Plugins:
    - **`live`** — Unified live-resource API, read half: useLive (a collection's window — where/orderBy/limit with canGrow/growing/loadMore — a grouping of a filterable column's values with counts, grown by its limit, a collection declared `all` whole — every row in its declared order, or a select-scoped slice of it — an explicit id set, or one row by id — `{ id }`: loading, failed, found, or determinately absent — all through one collection signature, so a wrong option errors on its own property), useLiveReader (the one read function beside useLive: one answer to one tuple of a liveValue, for a question an event asks and its own await consumes — its pushed value when observed, else one deduped HTTP read never written to the cache; refused / unavailable typed by the declaration), with mapRow reducing a row read to a ResourceResult of what the row means, RowView rendering one with a required not-found arm, and rowOrStale the one sanctioned reduction of it to the row as far as known (for a guarded pane body, a title, a chip); useLive also reads a typed-query liveValue (its question encoded to one canonical tuple); every collection's window — and a key-range-paged liveValue — is read as key-range pages — bounded windows tiling the order by server-minted row-key cuts, split when full and merged when small — given a measured viewport (useLive(c, q, { viewport })) with no depth limit, the pages near it live and the rest held stale up to a per-reader budget, past which they are height-keeping placeholders drawn before and after the rows, and without one every page live, capped at maxLimit rows; FieldPresentation.Register presents an owner's fields — an entity's own, an extension's exposed ones, a union arm's, a collection's own — with their cells, widths and live options in every list that reaches the owner, read by useFieldPresentations. Unified live-resource API, server half: serveValue (a liveValue's loader, from Postgres — change-feed driven — or from an external source with notify(); the serve call decides only the freshness, never the shape: every list's bound is the liveValue's own (its schema's list-bound markers), so a serve call takes no `unbounded`; pushed by default, or refetched over HTTP when the liveValue declares `load: "on-demand"`; a typed-query value's hooks and notify take the decoded question, and a key-range-paged one — external only — is loaded one key range at a time, each answer checked against its range and minted its `$key`, notify(q) reaching every subscribed page and the per-question meta sibling, and sliceRange answers a range for a list held in memory) and serveCollection (binds a liveCollection's row fields to a table's columns — the projection is exactly the row schema — ANDs an optional base `where` into every read, and compiles its window + `:rows` point resources through windowQueryResource and its `:groups` GROUP BY push value — only `:rows` for a lookup-only collection, and the whole ordered set (`key`, a routed scopedMembership alias compiled by compileAllCollection) + `:rows` for one declared `all` — encoding a column type's declared wire form in JS per row; a collection reaching an entity compiles at boot, folding every LiveColumns.Expose contribution of an extension exposing fields of it — and a `scopedColumns` collection every LiveColumns.Scoped set, in the scope each query names — into its rows' `$columns`; routed through the change feed, or — with `changes` — the same compiled SQL served off it, for a table its owner opted out) — or, `source: "external"`, from a source outside Postgres that answers window / rows / groups / count / all by hand (core's serveCollectionOn: every answer checked against the row schema, every window row's `$key` minted, notify() re-reading the subscribed tuples); every filter compiles through the filter language's filterSql. Unified live-resource API, central half: serveValue for a liveValue declared `origin: "central"` — the external arm only (central has no change feed), registered through the central plugin's `resources: [served]`; its options compile through the same code as the worktree serveValue.

        - **`change-feed`** — L4 DB change-feed: STATEMENT-level Postgres triggers that pg_notify on every commit, plus a LISTEN consumer routing each change through the live-state recompute cascade — making missed invalidations structurally impossible and out-of-process writes visible.         - **`live-state-snapshot`** — Registers the epoch handoff's switch (Hand live state over across restarts) for Settings → Config. L2 persisted live-state materialization: durable snapshot + xmin watermark for instant cold boot, served only from a usable row (a key the runtime persists now, under its current definition, from a current writer). Three persist modes (a FULL recompute replaces; a persisted alias's trailing window lowers the floor, or advances it to a routed cut once its snapshot is proven settled under one), an hourly compact job, and a boot catch-up that seeds each persisted alias from its row and replays the changelog by scope — or, when history was pruned past the floor or a rollup was healed, recomputes every persisted key.

Central's reach to the source-digest closure walk: closureChangedSince(entries, sinceMs) — whether nothing a closure loads (repo files, package resolution entries) changed since an instant, by inode change time — and sourceDigest(sets), the digest of the code a set loads.     - **`tags`** — Page tags, web half: the vocabulary and per-page reads (usePageTags, useListedPageTags off a listed row's exposed `tags`, the editable usePageTagsEditor), the soft TagChip / TagDot, the read-only PageTagChips, and the TagPicker popover (search or create, toggle, and per-tag rename / recolor / delete). Page tags, server half: the page_tags vocabulary and the page_blocks_ext_tags assignments (one ordered tag-id list per tagged page), both served live; the vocabulary CRUD and per-page PUT endpoints; and the reads/writes other plugins use — loadPageTags (the <page-meta> header), resolveTagNames (name → tag, refusing unknown names unless created explicitly) and writeResolvedPageTags / setPageTags. A page's tags are exposed as the `tags` field of every list whose rows are blocks (LiveColumns.Expose).

    - **`exhibits`** — Exhibit catalog: a plugin shows one of its REAL components standalone from an exhibits/ folder (isolatedExhibit / regionExhibit / appExhibit), collected into one generated registry. useExhibits() / useExhibit(id) answer loading / found / missing / ambiguous; <ExhibitView exhibit width?/> renders any arm inside its own error boundary. Debug → Exhibits lists the catalog as a DataView (searchable, grouped by id prefix, badged by runtime and geometry); a row opens the viewer pane (/debug/exhibit/<id>;theme=<app>) rendering that one exhibit at each of its widths inside an explicit, switchable theme boundary; its Open full-screen action opens the stage (/debug/exhibit-stage/<id>;width=<px>;theme=<app>), the exhibit alone over the whole tab.

    - **`relocate`** — `./equin plugin move <from> <to>` — relocate or rename a plugin (and every descendant) in one step: git mv the folder and its config dir, then rewrite every reference the plugin-refs locator finds (path literals, @plugins specifiers, dot ids, relative links) by exact range.     - **`action-presentation`** — The shrink-ladder seam between a widget and the bar that hosts it: useActionForm declares the smaller forms a widget can render ITSELF as (and how eagerly it yields room to its neighbours) and reads back the form the region assigned — one hook, both directions. A region can only hand a widget a form that widget declared, so a rich control can never be transformed into something it is not; PanelActionRow renders the 'row' rung, the one IconButton declares — a labelled row that stands alone in the always-mounted overflow panel, never a menu item.

        - **`working-dots`** — Three-dot working indicator with organic motion: <WorkingDots> varies each pass (duration, amplitude, lag) through smooth noise, carries the dots on springs with a faint overshoot and stretch, holds between passes with a breath, and cycles through every style (gooey, wave, leap, orbit, ring, glow). Alive to the pointer: the nearest dot reaches toward a pointer at the row, and a poke draws a varied reaction (scatter, hop, gulp, shiver, bolt, spin). Sized from the ambient ControlSize; pauses off screen; still under reduced motion. <WorkingText> is the label beside it: a highlight sweeping across the words, each new label sliding in.

      - Test helpers:
        - Web: `@plugins/primitives/plugins/data-view/web/testing`
          - `consumerPaging` — A consumer's paging (`DataViewProps.paging`): placeholders before and after the rows, every viewport report pushed to `reports`, nothing to grow.
          - `deriveFields` — {@link useDerivedFields}, pure.
          - `describePagedConformance` — The paged-view contract every DataView view honours, run against `view` mounted through the real body on a laid-out page (`mountPagedDataView`):
          - `isFieldValueEmpty` — Whether `field` has nothing to show for `row` — THE empty test, shared by the table's edit affordance (an empty editable cell offers its pencil over an "Empty" placeholder) and the card / list meta (an empty field is simply omitted, never drawn as "Empty").
          - `lowerFilterGroup` — Lower a DataView `FilterGroup` into a filter-language `Filter`, each rule through its operator's `lower` with `ctx.column` = the field id.
          - `lowersToMatch` — Does a rule `op(operand)` keep a row whose field projects to `value`? — the in-memory evaluator's exact path for one rule: `op.lower` over a column of `domain` (an incomplete rule, `undefined`, keeps every row), the DataView domain adapter, then the filter language's `matchesFilter`.
          - `mountPagedDataView` — Mount ONE view of a paged DataView against a laid-out page — through the real seam (`DataViewShellFrame` around `DataViewBody`, the body every DataView renders), with a fake one-instance view model, inside a scroller whose `scrollTop` the test drives and an IntersectionObserver that answers from the layout, as a browser does.
          - `PAGED_VIEWPORT_PX` — The scroller's visible height.
          - `renameColumns` — Rename every clause's column through `rename` (field id → column name).
          - `resolveLiveFields` — Resolve a schema against a live source — and check it where it is declared.
          - `testField` — A minimal option-less field for a test that calls `op.lower` directly.
          - Types: `PagedDataView`, `PagedLayout`, `PagedViewUnderTest`

        - **`after-layout`** — Read layout where the browser already computed it: afterLayout(read) runs `read` once the current frame is styled and laid out, before it paints (a ResizeObserver delivery), batched with every other read of that frame — reads first, then the writes they return, then one React commit (flushSync) — so a layout or style read never forces a synchronous recalc on React's commit path, and a write never sits between two reads. runAsAfterLayout(fn, delivered) lets a ResizeObserver callback join the phase; commitInPhase(update) is its one way to commit before paint — whatever that commit resizes at or above the delivery (which the browser could only deliver a frame late, with a 'ResizeObserver loop' error) is answered in the same phase through the observer's onHeldBack, and its observation restarted at the next frame; observeInPhase(observer, el, onHeldBack?) starts and keeps an observation where the browser can deliver it — at once, or (a target the running delivery can no longer reach) at the next frame — and arms the root trigger with one started outside a phase, so its first callback shares the root's broadcast. element-size and layout-host read through it.

        - **`copy-source-text`** — Copy what an element STANDS FOR, not only what it shows: an element declares its source text via copiesAsText() / copiesAsOwnText — exported beside the handler, so importing them ships it — and one Core.Root-mounted document copy handler swaps every declaring element in the selection for that text before re-serializing the clipboard through the browser's own block-aware serializer. Restores the characters a rendering replaced (an active-data chip's `token`), and removes the newlines a chip's blockified label box injects mid-sentence. Yields to any handler that already prevented the default, and never acts inside a contenteditable. A substituting element also SELECTS as one unit: its letters take no highlight, and a selectionchange listener rings the whole element while the selection overlaps it — so the selection shows exactly what the copy will carry.

    - **`metrics`** — Metrics surfaces: useMetricCatalog / useMetric / useMetricDetails / useMetricDetailsTotal (live reads of the served metrics values — the details one key-range pages, every loaded one live, and its total the per-question meta sibling — so a change the metric's source announces refetches what is on screen, without polling), MetricTile (KPI toggle with value, polarity-coloured delta and sparkline), MetricCard (controls derived from the catalog entry: split, daily | cumulative for flows, table twin, previous-period line on the unsplit total), BreakdownCard, RangeBar, the DrillDrawer listing the records behind a bucket, BoardView (sections of focus tiles, a lead card and a card grid, every ref checked against the catalog) and Board (a view-core tabbed board whose specs live in a config declared with defineBoardConfig). Metrics engine: the MetricsServer.Source contribution (a source's metrics and breakdowns bound to their evaluators), the served metrics.catalog / metrics.query / metrics.details live values evaluating any of them through the one tz-aware bucketing engine — each query and drill-down (its key-range pages and its total) watching its source's `changes` through one refcounted subscription per source — and the sqlFlow / sqlLevel helpers joining a table against the engine's intervals.

          - `createTransportHub` — Compose one server + worker registry + lock manager into a multi-tab transport.
          - `FakeLockManager` — A `navigator.locks`-shaped exclusive lock, promise-based like the real API.
          - `FakeMessagePort` — One end of an entangled `MessageChannel`. `postMessage` delivers a `structuredClone` to the other end on a REAL microtask.
          - `FakePageLifecycle` — A page's `pagehide` / `pageshow` events, fired by hand.
          - `FakeSharedWorkers` — The browser's SharedWorker registry: one REAL `createSharedWsHost` per worker name (the production worker's logic, in-process), shared by every tab; `make(name)` is the `makeSharedWorker` factory, connecting a fresh `MessageChannel` to that host like the worker's `connect` event.
          - `FakeWebSocket` — A `WebSocketLike` with no network.
          - `FakeWsServer` — A no-network WebSocket server: `connect` is the bound `makeWebSocket` factory; every socket it ever handed out is retained for introspection (`all`), and the currently-OPEN subset (`openSockets`) is derived live from `readyState` so it is the single source of truth for the one-socket invariant.
          - `renderWithTransport` — `render(ui)` under a `<TransportProvider>` — what every component reading `useTransport()` (the endpoints hooks, `useLive`) needs, since the context has no default.
          - `testTransport` — A page-shaped transport for a test: same-origin sockets (`SharedWebSocket`), the global `fetch` read at call time (so a fetch the test stubs answers), assets loaded by their own path, no request timing (a stubbed fetch has no Resource Timing entry), the computer behind it, and its telemetry reported — each overridable.
          - `transportWrapper` — A `wrapper` (`render` / `renderHook`) mounting `transport` above the tree.
          - Types: `FakeWsServerOptions`, `RenderWithTransportOptions`, `TabHandle`, `TransportHub`

    - **`undo-redo`** — Surface-scoped client-side undo/redo command-history stack: a UndoRedoProvider per surface tab holding past/future stacks of {undo,redo} thunks, with time-windowed coalescing, a max-depth cap, a re-entrancy guard so replayed patches aren't re-recorded, mount-scoped entries (useScopedUndoRedo drops its entries when its mount unmounts), a pending-flush seam (usePendingFlush / registerPendingFlush: a producer holding a not-yet-recorded entry seals it at the start of every undo/redo turn, outside the replay guard, so it is the entry popped), serialized turns (an undo/redo during an in-flight thunk queues FIFO behind it instead of running under the guard), and an optional useUndoRedoShortcuts (mod+z / mod+shift+z / mod+y) convenience binding.

    - **`usage-rank`** — Frecency usage ranking for any (namespace, key) set: useRecordUsage() returns the recorder that fires one atomic decay-and-increment, useUsageOrder() returns the most-used-first order — one coalesced id-set subscription, frozen per context so chips never move under the cursor, seeded from a local cache so the first paint does not re-sort — and useRecentUsage() lists a namespace's most recently used keys (a bounded window), for a Recent row with no candidate set to rank. Owns the usage_stats table: one frecency rollup per (namespace, key), updated by a single atomic decay-and-increment upsert, served as a lookup-only live collection read by id set, and the nightly sweep of keys unused for a year.

Adaptive-bar report kind: validates the adaptive-bar primitive's layout-contract fault payloads (no-slack = the bar was given no room to give, nested-bar = a measuring bar was written inside another bar's occupant so both claim the same row's slack, row-overflow = on a converged pass the fit blessed the row as fitting and the occupants still stick out of the bar's own content box, no-convergence = the placement never settled, iframe-relocation = a frame the browser cannot move without reloading, empty-rung = a widget declared a smaller form and rendered nothing as it), fingerprints by fault + origin (the innermost UI-context node above the bar's root, falling back to the label that several unrelated bars share) + overflow mode + the offending occupant's id, excluding the per-occurrence lineage path, round evidence and message so one broken bar = one row, and renders a per-fault task — what the bar did instead, the consumer-side fix, and for no-convergence the recorded rounds naming which occupant resized itself. Re-arms periodically (6h) since a broken host re-produces the fault on every mount.

Check-thread-stall report kind: validates the check runner's thread-stall payloads (trigger stall = one stall whose code held the thread ≥ 2 s — held, not merely late: a starved thread files nothing —, fingerprinted by its top owner; trigger total = a run whose stalls add up to ≥ 20 s held, one row), filed through the report outbox, and renders a task naming the owner, its stacks, the held-vs-starved split and the run's transcript.     - **`main-thread-stall`** — Main-thread stall detector: a Core.Root controller that attaches each tab to one out-of-thread SharedWorker watchdog (1 Hz ping, Web Lock per tab, IndexedDB record of an open stall) and feeds it the tab's app, route pattern, visibility and LoAF long frames; a visible tab silent ≥5 s becomes a main-thread-stall report plus a slow-op span (recovered 1–5 s long frames: slow-op only). In-tab fallback without SharedWorker. Slow interactions: Event Timing (input → next paint) per click / key press, its target resolved at dispatch (element, contribution, pane, component), its time split by the long frames inside it; ≥200 ms is an `interaction` slow-op, severe (≥800 ms) or recurring (3× ≥300 ms) a slow-interaction report, and it owns the 1–5 s long frame it caused. Main-thread-stall report kind: validates the stall payload (tab, app, route pattern, duration, how it ended, LoAF attribution, cohort), fingerprints by the interaction's target when a click / key press started the freeze, else by app + route pattern + top attributed function, and renders the investigation task. Slow-interaction report kind: a click / key press whose next paint came late, fingerprinted by what was interacted with (element, contribution, pane, component — never the app or route), its time split into script / forced style-layout / style-layout / other with the function that forced it.
