- **`runs`** — The merged run surface: <RunsDataView> over the `runs` union window (a live scroll: base fields derived from the collection and presented once, plus every arm's own fields, derived from its liveArm, each bound to its column), and the seams an arm reaches it through: runLinks (where its rows go — data-view's CollectionRowActivation over the arm), investigateRuns; the kind filter's options are the registered arms, derived by every list; an arm presents its fields' cells with FieldPresentation.Register({ owner: arm }). Every row is a single field-driven line; a domain's detail lives in the pane its rows open. Also exports useRun (a live point read of one run by its (kind, id) pair). The merged run space as ONE routed union window (a Meta-DataView): runsServed serves the `runs` collection's window, its `:rows` point read (useRun) and `:groups` from every arm bound through runsServed.arm — a domain's own ledger typed against the base row and its liveArm, the ledger id and the duration derived by the union — so a write to one ledger refills only the rows it changed. Names no run kind.

    - **`toast`** — Global toast notifications: a plain showToast() (text toasts: data only) backed by sonner's global API, and useShowCustomToast() — a toast whose content the caller draws, rendered in the caller's render origin (its transport, registry and navigator) while the stack only places it, plus the Core.Root-mounted sonner Toaster host. Degrades to a silent no-op when no host is mounted. A toast declaring audience developer is shown only in Developer mode. useSuppressToasts() lets a surface that is its whole document (the menu-bar panel) turn the host off while mounted.

- **`tag-tree`** — Umbrella for nested tag trees: one per-plugin table of tags (name, parent, colour, icon, fractional rank) declared in three lines, served through one endpoint set, and picked, created, renamed, recoloured, nested and reordered in one shared picker.
  - Plugins:
    - **`engine`** — Tag-tree engine (web): useTagTree reads a declared tree live (the whole tree, in rank order) and useTagTreeActions binds the engine's create / create-path / update / move / delete endpoints to it. Tag-tree engine (server): defineTagTreeTable builds a tree's table from its ref, serveTagTree + the TagTrees.Tree contribution register a tree with its carriers, and the ONE /api/tag-trees/:tree endpoint set writes any registered tree under a table lock — create (unique sibling names, appended rank), create path, update, move (positional intent, cycles refused) and delete (children lifted to the parent at the tag's position, carriers rewritten).

    - **`automations`** — Automations in the agent manager: the Automations sidebar entry and list (a DataView over the catalog — trigger in words, next run, on/off, open task), the detail pane (Run now through Background activity; Behavior — enabled, model, push policy; Trigger — schedule presets or custom cron, or the event and its settle wait; the sections an automation contributes through Automations.Section; its sources; the Prompt template with Customized / Reset to default — PromptTemplateBlock, the same editor for any template field an automation declares; and the History of the tasks it filed or started — each row expandable into the Automations.TaskDetail contributions for its task), the presentation of the exposed `origin` Automation field (its options the live catalog) and `approval` Approval field (Approved / Excluded / Not approved) in every list whose rows reach a task, useTaskApproval / useSetTaskApproval — one task's launch decision, read and written from the task, and automationConfigContributions — how a declaring plugin registers its automation's config document (Automations.Config). Automations registry: defineAutomation declares something that files a task and launches its agent on its own (file kind) or launches agents on existing tasks a few at a time (launch kind: candidates, launched ONLY when a person approved them — the tasks_ext_launch_decision side-table, one decision per task whatever automation launches it, written by the decide-launch and task-approval endpoints alone — concurrency slots held until a task settles or its agent reports — the automations.slot code watcher on every launched task, fed the outcome report and the task's settled / stopped / held facts through the watch plugin —, and a maxLaunches batch per turn-on after which it turns itself off), and owns its job (automation.<id>) — its config document (defineAutomationConfig: enabled, push policy, model, excluded sources, trigger — a schedule re-installed live on change, or an event whose bursts settle into one run — and the prompt template), the one-open-task dedupe (and, for a file automation whose `watch` is refire, the automations.refire code watcher on each filed task, running it again as soon as that task settles), the filled prompt, the filing (task + category + tasks_ext_origin row in one transaction) and the armed launch. Serves the automations.launch-decisions.all set, exposes the filing automation and the launch decision to every list whose rows reach a task (the `origin` and `approval` fields), and notifies the bell when an automated task needs its person. The automations.catalog value and the automations.tasks collection (the origin side-table, an automation's history) are the machine half's.

    - **`sidequest-autopilot`** — The Sidequest autopilot in the Automations pane: registers its config (enabled, at once, in total, push policy, model, prompt, triage) and contributes its sections — Launch list (a DataView of every ready sidequest in launch order — triage's priority, then oldest — grouped Approved / Proposed by triage / Needs your call / Looks obsolete / won't / Triage failed / Triaging / Excluded; each row shows its priority and type, and expands to triage's context, its one-click question and Re-triage; triage may tick a row, only Approve selected approves), Run until (until you turn it off, or until a date and time after which it turns itself off) and Triage (whether new sidequests are triaged automatically). Declares the Sidequest autopilot automation (launch kind, off by default): while on, it starts agents on the ready sidequests (no attempt, not held, dropped or blocked) a person APPROVED — best first by triage's priority (must → should → could, then oldest filed), `concurrency` at a time (default 2), at most `maxLaunches` per turn-on (default 5) — each with the autopilot prompt (triage's context, the person's answer and their note included; never ask, check obsolescence first, stay in scope, push only what the push policy allows, finish with submit_outcome_report). Triage is task-triage's: while the `triage` toggle is on (default, main only) it asks task-triage for a read of each ready sidequest that has none — when a task becomes a sidequest or a sidequest becomes ready, backfilled at boot and when the toggle turns on. Triage approves nothing. Turns itself off at its `runUntil`.

    - **`task-triage`** — The Triage card in the task detail: the state chip and when it ran (or its place in the queue) in the header, with Conversation (the run's, for follow-up questions) and Re-run; the body per state — Run triage when none, a placeholder while queued or running, the read (Verdict · Priority · Type · Risk, the summary, one question with one-click answers), greyed under a Re-run notice when stale, the error with Re-run when failed — then the person's autosaved note and the Approve / ✓ Approved toggle, which needs no triage. Presents the exposed Triage, Priority, Type and Last triaged fields in every task list, and registers the triage config (its model picked from the live model catalog). Owns task triage: the tasks_ext_triage side-table (one read per task — run state queued / running / done / stale / failed, verdict, MoSCoW priority, type, risk, context, one one-click question) and tasks_ext_triage_note (the person's note, fed to every run). A run is a read-only `system` conversation in a `tasks.triage` scratch workspace (Edit / Write / NotebookEdit / Bash denied) under the triaged task's own `Triage: …` run task (System category, subject `task-triage`), reporting through its task_submit_triage MCP tool; a dispatcher job launches queued runs `concurrency` at a time. A read goes stale when the task's text changes or after `staleAfterDays`; a run whose conversation closes without a read, or that has not submitted after 30 min, fails. Exposes Triage, Priority, Type and Last triaged to every list of tasks; requestTriage is the API other plugins queue a read with.

    - **`icons`** — Draws icons: <Icon icon={symbol(…)} active?/> renders an IconRef from the page's inline SVG sprites in its theme scope's icon style. A leaf below the ui-kit — it knows no theme: the icons token group publishes each scope's style (usePublishIconStyle), <Theme> boundaries say which scope an icon is in (IconScopeProvider), and the sprites plugin fills and mounts the sheet. Icon families beyond Material are contributed to Icons.Family (Lucide is this plugin's own; an app draws its own with defineIconFamily), published to <Icon> by IconFamilyHost. A family states its coverage: fallback (an unmapped symbol draws the next family of its chain, Material last) or strict (its gap glyph, reported through iconFamilyGapReportSink); resolveIconSource answers which, by the same chain. A held sprite without an icon's symbol (the build's manifest missed its name) draws a crossed-out missing-glyph marker and is reported through iconMissingGlyphReportSink — never a silent empty box. Animated family glyphs (data-motion parts, a closed ICON_MOTIONS vocabulary) are drawn inline and play once on hover inside an IconMotionRegion. The vendored Seti file-type set (jesseweed/seti-ui, MIT, one colour), portable: SETI_SET names it, readSetiSet loads it (a lazy JSON module, so a browser host bundles it too). The pure drawing — resolveIcon, resolveSymbol, buildSymbol — is core's; reading the installed Material sets is the machine half's (symbolBody).
      - Web:
        - Slots:
          - `Icons.Root`
          - `Icons.Family`
        - Slot contributors:
          - `Icons.Root` ← `ui.icons`
          - `Icons.Root` ← `ui.icons.sprites`
          - `Icons.Root` ← `ui.tokens.icons`
          - `Icons.Family` ← `apps.agent-manager.icons`

        - **`sprites`** — Mounts the page's icon sprites inline: the resident default-style sprites from the boot snapshot (present at first paint) plus, on demand, the sprite of every other style a theme scope picks, and the page's saved-icon symbols. ScopeIconSymbols gives a plugin scope (a demo) saved icons of its own, read from the scope's server and drawn in a sheet inside it. The build's sprites on demand, on every host: icons.sprite (one sprite by key, immutable, content-addressed by icons.sprite-hash) drawn through the host's SpriteDrawer — the computer's installed sets (this plugin's machine half) or the Seti and Lucide sets bundled with a browser host (plugins/bundled-sprites) — so a scope reads its sprites from its own server. Saved (user-picked) icons as runtime symbols, on every host: the resident icons.saved-sprites value draws every name a saved-icon source (ui/icons/saved-sources) reports in the default style, and the on-demand icons.runtime-symbols value serves any saved names in any style, immutable (content-addressed by symbolsHash). Both draw through the host's RuntimeSymbolDrawer — the icon sets installed on the computer (this plugin's machine half), or a set bundled with the page (plugins/bundled-symbols, a browser host) — so a demo's icons come from its own server.

    - **`theme-engine`** — Paints each scope's selected theme: the token-group, theme and theme-source slots, the theme selection config, the injector that resolves one theme per scope into CSS variables, and light/dark per region: every app wears its own effective color mode (the app's declared default from defineApp, the user's per-app override, else the global setting) on its own boundary, published for theme-boundary to stamp (ColorSchemePublisher), each fixed theme its own scheme, and <html> the desktop's — so a focus or surface-mode change flips no scheme. The light/dark controls read and write the focused full-surface app's setting through useColorModeSetting (a state: not known until the surface says which app fills it); useColorMode is the scheme of the region a component renders in. :root always wears the desktop's theme; each app's theme is painted on its own scope. Registers the theme selection and per-app color-mode configs, and paints the first frame: renders the page's first-frame theme CSS (:root, the canvas and the opened app's scope) into the SPA shell's head (DocumentHead.Fragment) from the generated theme declarations, the ThemeEngine.Source themes, the selections and each app's effective light/dark (its declared default and the user's override), re-rendered when any of them changes.
      - Web:

          - `ThemeEngine.TokenGroup`

- **`upstream`** — Registers the Upstream merges automation's config (schedule, push policy, model, prompt template) for the Automations pane and Settings → Config. Daily upstream.detect-updates job (main only): when the repo this checkout was cloned from has commits local `main` does not, it records one rolling `upstream-updates-available` report — the bell and Debug → Reports, whose Investigate mints a merge task. And the Upstream merges automation (upstream-merge; off by default, daily once on, editable from the Automations pane): when upstream is ahead and no merge task is open, it files ONE auto-started task (Upstream category, linked to the report) whose agent runs `./equin upstream merge`, builds and checks the app, and lands it only as far as its Push setting allows (never, by default).
